bundleSuggestion: Universal expansion — pairs with any Kayfabizarro deck; Moods/Skills/Powers/Tools tier explicitly designed to shuffle into existing decks.

cards.power: Stasis Loop. Play this to cancel any Quest progression this turn. Narrate why nothing can change.
cards.lore: Dysfunction isn't just a state; it's a habit. We normalize the abnormal until the extraordinary seems impossible.
cards.gradeReason: Canceling Quest IS the stasis — mechanic mirrors the psychology exactly. Zero gap.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-watercolor. Subject: rabbit frozen in grey domestic routine loop. Mood: comfortable numbness.

cards.power: Cognitive Dissonance. Increase Quest Die by +1. Force another player to introduce a conflict that disrupts their current plans.
cards.lore: The universe doesn't knock. It throws a brick. The disruption of normalcy is always the beginning.
cards.gradeReason: You ARE the disruption — forcing another player to break their story is pure performative chaos.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-watercolor. Subject: rabbit startled by cosmic brick crashing through a window. Mood: electric shock.

cards.power: Rational Panic. Pause the Quest for one turn. All players must explain why they can't possibly go on the adventure.
cards.lore: Fear is realistic self-preservation. Change means death of the familiar self. The familiar self is terrible at math.
cards.gradeReason: Everyone voices their avoidance aloud — collective embodied improv from a single mechanic. Ensemble gold.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-watercolor. Subject: rabbit backing away from glowing open door, arms crossed. Mood: fearful hesitation.

cards.power: External Hard Drive. Draw 2 cards. Give 1 to another player. Wisdom is useless until it's shared.
cards.lore: The Mentor cannot go with you. They provide the map, not the legs.
cards.gradeReason: Draw-and-give mechanic enacts the wisdom transfer — can't keep the map, only share it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-watercolor. Subject: elder rabbit handing a scroll to young rabbit. Mood: bittersweet generosity.

cards.power: Point of No Return. Move Quest Die +2. Discard your hand and draw 3 new cards. The old world is gone.
cards.lore: Commitment is the moment fear becomes movement. You can't un-take the step.
cards.gradeReason: Discard your hand — you literally can't go back. Commitment as mechanical irreversibility.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-watercolor. Subject: rabbit mid-leap over flaming threshold line. Mood: terrifying elation.

cards.power: Digestion. All players discard 1 card. No Quest progress this turn. Next turn, the Quest Die doubles.
cards.lore: Liminal space. No longer who you were, not yet who you'll become.
cards.gradeReason: All players pause with you — collective liminal suspension enacted at the table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-watercolor. Subject: rabbit curled inside dark whale belly, faint light ahead. Mood: suspended dissolution.

cards.power: Grindset. Narrate 3 small problems. For each one you 'solve' in the fiction, gain +1 to your next roll.
cards.lore: Recovery is practice. The hero who survives the trials is not the hero who entered them.
cards.gradeReason: Name three problems, solve them in fiction — grindset as narrative accumulation. Improv workout.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-watercolor. Subject: rabbit trudging uphill path strewn with small obstacles. Mood: exhausted determination.

cards.power: Self-Love Bomb. Narrate a moment of acceptance. Quest Die +1 for every player who agrees you deserve it.
cards.lore: The experience of being fully seen. The internal integration of opposites into unconditional love.
cards.gradeReason: Other players vote your acceptance — the whole table performs the therapeutic moment together.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-watercolor. Subject: rabbit bathed in radiant feminine light, arms wide open. Mood: overwhelming acceptance.

cards.power: Regression Pull. Tempt another player to discard a 'Safety' card. If they do, they gain a reward but lose 2 on the Quest Die.
cards.lore: The siren song of comfort. The familiar cage feels safer than the unknown field.
cards.gradeReason: You ARE the temptation — player must perform seduction of another player's regression.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-watercolor. Subject: cozy comfort-trap cage with soft pillow, door invitingly ajar. Mood: seductive regression.

cards.power: Daddy Issues. Identify an Authority Card on the Stage. Destroy it or Integrate it. Both options work differently.
cards.lore: Confront the source of authority. Kill the internal 'should' to find the authentic 'want.'
cards.gradeReason: Destroy or Integrate — player chooses how to handle authority. Binary decision IS the scene.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-watercolor. Subject: rabbit facing giant stern authority figure, scissors in one paw. Mood: confrontational catharsis.

cards.power: Ego Death. Discard your Actor Marker. You are now a Formlessness. You may intervene in any scene as a nameless force.
cards.lore: The caterpillar is liquid. The butterfly is inevitable.
cards.gradeReason: Discard your identity marker — dissolution of self as literal mechanical act. Most existential move in deck.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-watercolor. Subject: rabbit dissolving into spiral light, actor marker floating away. Mood: terrifying transcendence.

cards.power: The Elixir. Gain a permanent 'Treasure' token. Use it once to auto-succeed on any Quest roll.
cards.lore: Integration of the lesson. It's not the object, it's the internal shift the object represents.
cards.gradeReason: Permanent Treasure token — reward as embodied integration, not just a mechanical bonus.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-watercolor. Subject: glowing elixir bottle held aloft in triumphant rabbit paw. Mood: quiet triumph.

cards.power: Stay in Narnia. You may choose to end the game for your Actor here. They do not return. They transcend.
cards.lore: Why go back to the mundane when you've touched the transcendent? The ordinary world is terrible by comparison.
cards.gradeReason: Staying is a real game choice — refusing return as honorable actor exit.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-watercolor. Subject: rabbit at portal edge looking back at luminous magical world. Mood: reluctant transcendence.

cards.power: Escape Velocity. End the Quest immediately. Roll a D6. Even: You keep the Boon. Odd: The Boon is lost in transit.
cards.lore: Old patterns don't release easily. The ego will chase you to the threshold.
cards.gradeReason: Gamble your Boon on escape — tension of whether the transformation survives the return.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-watercolor. Subject: rabbit sprinting, old shadow-self reaching from behind. Mood: desperate velocity.

cards.power: Intervention. Play this on another player who is stuck. You automatically provide the next card they need.
cards.lore: You can't do it all alone. Community is necessary. Independence is a trauma response.
cards.gradeReason: Mechanical community act — you intervene in another player's story. Corpus-best lore line.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-watercolor. Subject: rabbit hand reaching down to lift another rabbit from a pit. Mood: communal grace.

cards.power: Re-Entry Shock. Draw 1 card for yourself, give 1 to a neighbor. The gift must be explained in character.
cards.lore: The hardest stage. Can you maintain your transformation while re-entering the old context?
cards.gradeReason: Gift explained in character — re-entry shock as in-fiction social performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-watercolor. Subject: rabbit stepping back through gate carrying a gift box. Mood: re-entry shock.

cards.power: Code Switch. You may play cards from the Discard Pile as if they were in your hand for this turn.
cards.lore: No split between 'spiritual' and 'mundane.' You are whole. You are both.
cards.gradeReason: Play from discard — mechanical integration of past into present. Wholeness as game power.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-watercolor. Subject: rabbit standing at crossroads of two worlds, grounded and luminous. Mood: integrated wholeness.

cards.power: Zen Mode. Your Actor becomes a Mentor. You cannot lose. You just vibe.
cards.lore: Freedom from the tyranny of fear. You're alive. That's enough.
cards.gradeReason: Cannot lose, just vibe — Zen as game state. Shortest, most complete performance invitation.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-watercolor. Subject: rabbit in lotus pose, cards floating serenely around. Mood: effortless liberation.

cards.power: Tragedy of Stagnation. Cancel a 'Call to Adventure.' Nothing happens. The story ends before it begins.
cards.lore: Many refuse the call until they die. This is not a moral failure, it is a statistical reality.
cards.gradeReason: [R:0][A:0][F:0] — nothing happens IS the performance. Tragedy made into a playable mechanic.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-watercolor. Subject: rabbit standing at threshold, turning away, world going flat grey. Mood: quiet tragedy.

cards.power: Eternal Recurrence. Reset the Quest Die to [3]. Start the exact same story over, but you know it now.
cards.lore: The spiral goes up. Or down. But it definitely goes around.
cards.gradeReason: [R:6][A:6][F:6] — same story again, spiral confirmed. Eternal return as reset.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-watercolor. Subject: rabbit on infinite spiral staircase, same glowing door at every level. Mood: vertiginous infinity.

cards.power: Main Character Energy. You may re-roll the Quest Die once per turn.
cards.lore: The one who transforms. The ego vehicle. Often confused, usually earnest, always the protagonist.
cards.gradeReason: Re-roll once per turn — protagonist privilege as embodied mechanic.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-watercolor. Subject: rabbit in heroic stance, dice glowing in paw. Mood: confused confidence.

cards.power: Projection. Force another player to face a negative consequence you were supposed to face.
cards.lore: The dark mirror. The antagonist is just the part of you that you haven't accepted yet.
cards.gradeReason: Force another player to face what you avoided — projection as literal game mechanic.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-watercolor. Subject: rabbit casting dark mirror-shadow that lunges toward another player. Mood: confrontational darkness.

cards.power: Trust Issues. Change the 'Suit' or 'Type' of any card on the Stage.
cards.lore: Loyalty is ambiguous. Keeps the hero off-balance. Is it love or is it strategy?
cards.gradeReason: Change any card's type — ambiguity is literally a tool you wield at the table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-watercolor. Subject: rabbit with shifting multiple faces, cards morphing mid-air. Mood: unsettling fluidity.

cards.power: Wake Up Call. Play immediately when a Quest ends to start a new one automatically.
cards.lore: Brings the Call. The Inciting Incident personified. Annoying, but structurally necessary.
cards.gradeReason: Instant new Quest — you ARE the next inciting incident. Herald as mechanic.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-watercolor. Subject: rabbit blowing trumpet at closed door, new quest scroll unfurling. Mood: insistent disruption.

cards.power: Gatekeeping. Block a player from playing a card on the Stage unless they justify it in character.
cards.lore: Tests the hero's resolve. If you can't get past the doorman, you don't get in.
cards.gradeReason: Block unless they perform justification in-character — gatekeeping as improv demand.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-watercolor. Subject: armored rabbit blocking stone archway, arms folded. Mood: stern challenge.

cards.power: Chaos Agent. Swap the hands of two players. Laugh.
cards.lore: Disrupts the status quo. Reveals truth through absurdity. Also, very annoying at parties.
cards.gradeReason: Swap hands. Laugh. Full stop. Chaos as one-sentence performance instruction. Corpus best mechanic.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-watercolor. Subject: grinning rabbit juggling cards between two bewildered players. Mood: joyful chaos.

cards.power: Emotional Support. Add +1 to any die roll made by another player.
cards.lore: You need a Samwise. Someone to carry the load when you can't.
cards.gradeReason: +1 to another's roll — mechanical Samwise, shows up exactly when needed.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-watercolor. Subject: small rabbit beside larger rabbit, quiet supportive presence. Mood: steadfast warmth.

cards.power: The Bad Ending. Collapse the Quest immediately. No one gets a Boon.
cards.lore: The Ordeal can break you. Trauma can win. Not all stories have happy endings.
cards.gradeReason: Bad ending as real game outcome — not a reset, an honest defeat. Rare courage in card design.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-watercolor. Subject: rabbit kneeling in rubble of collapsed quest, treasure chest empty. Mood: honest defeat.

cards.power: Pressure Cooker. Use this card to set the limits [1] and [6]. If it tips, the reality breaks.
cards.lore: Chaos is a valid game state. If the die tips, the reality breaks.
cards.gradeReason: Engine card — describes the mechanic rather than inviting a performance. Clear but not Grade 1.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-watercolor. Subject: oversized die balanced on seesaw between order and chaos. Mood: precarious tension.

cards.power: Nonsense Check. Play anytime. Force the narrator to pause, clarify, and fix a logic failure. Then laugh.
cards.lore: 'It is not an accusation. It is a reset button. Laughter breaks nothing.'
cards.gradeReason: Force a pause AND laugh — reset button as community performance act. Structurally necessary.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-watercolor. Subject: rabbit holding giant red BLÖDSINN! button with theatrical authority. Mood: absurd authority.

cards.power: Suspension of Disbelief. Treat a lie as truth for the rest of the game.
cards.lore: The portrayal of staged events as real. We are all working the gimmick.
cards.gradeReason: Treat a lie as truth — the entire Kayfabizarro premise compressed into one card power.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-watercolor. Subject: rabbit winking behind theatrical curtain, REAL sign visible. Mood: conspiratorial delight.

cards.power: The Author. Change one rule of the game for this turn only.
cards.lore: 'I didn't finish this game. That part's yours. Stay fluffy.'
cards.gradeReason: Author breaks the fourth wall as a playable card — Hofstadter's Strange Loop in card form.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-watercolor. Subject: FrizzleBob holding scissors and pencil, winking at viewer. Mood: meta self-awareness.

cards.power: Paralysis. You cannot initiate a Quest. You can only react.
cards.lore: The cave you fear to enter holds the treasure. But the cave is very dark.
cards.gradeReason: Can only react — fear as embodied mechanical constraint. Player must perform reactive hesitation.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-watercolor. Subject: rabbit frozen mid-step, wide eyes, dark tunnel entrance looming. Mood: paralyzed dread.

cards.power: Leeroy Jenkins. You must play the first card you touch. No thinking allowed.
cards.lore: Action without thought. Sometimes it's bravery, sometimes it's a wall.
cards.gradeReason: First card you touch, you play — recklessness as mandatory improv constraint. No room to hedge.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-watercolor. Subject: rabbit mid-sprint, cards flying everywhere, zero hesitation. Mood: kinetic bravado.

cards.power: Heavy Heart. You cannot win a Boon this turn.
cards.lore: Loss is the price of love. The only way out is through.
cards.gradeReason: Purely restrictive with no performance direction — blocks but doesn't invite. Needs improv cue added.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-watercolor. Subject: rabbit hunched under grey cloud, holding single wilted card. Mood: heavy sorrow.

cards.power: Zoomies. Play 2 cards in one turn. Speak twice as fast.
cards.lore: Energy without direction. A brilliant disaster.
cards.gradeReason: Play 2 cards, speak twice as fast — mania as a literal physical performance instruction.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-watercolor. Subject: rabbit vibrating with energy, multiple cards in motion blur. Mood: brilliant frenetic chaos.

cards.power: Structure. You may rearrange the order of the Scenes on the Stage.
cards.lore: 'If it's stupid but it works, it's still stupid, but at least it works.'
cards.gradeReason: Rearrange Scenes — structure as immediate physical act at the table. Hands-on performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-watercolor. Subject: rabbit blueprinting card layout with compass and ruler. Mood: methodical creativity.

cards.power: Cut. Remove an unwanted card from the Stage.
cards.lore: 'Sometimes the Gordian Knot just needs a sharp edge.'
cards.gradeReason: Remove one card — the Cut as the cleanest, most decisive mechanic in the deck.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-watercolor. Subject: rabbit slicing card in two with elegant sword stroke. Mood: decisive clarity.

cards.power: Chill. Prevent a 'Kayfa-BOOM' (Quest Collapse) by negotiating the Die back into safe range.
cards.lore: 'The art of telling someone to go to hell in such a way that they look forward to the trip.'
cards.gradeReason: Social performance prevents mechanical collapse — diplomacy as literal survival act at the table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-watercolor. Subject: rabbit at round table, hands spread wide in negotiation. Mood: calm authority.

cards.power: Yoink. Steal a card from another player's hand.
cards.lore: 'Property is theft. Theft is also theft. It's complicated.'
cards.gradeReason: Steal a card with theatrical flourish — lore justification built into the act.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-watercolor. Subject: rabbit slipping card from another's hand with theatrical flourish. Mood: cheeky transgression.

cards.power: Retcon. Undo the last turn completely. It never happened.
cards.lore: The past is fluid. Memory is a creative act.
cards.gradeReason: Undo the last turn — retcon as literal game power. Past is fluid.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-watercolor. Subject: rabbit rewinding time-dial, cards floating in reverse. Mood: eerie temporal authority.

cards.power: Edit. Change the text on a Quest card.
cards.lore: Reality is a draft. Feel free to mark it up.
cards.gradeReason: Change card text — reality as draft, you are the editor. Most meta-creative power in deck.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-watercolor. Subject: rabbit with red pen marking up oversized playing card. Mood: editorial power.

cards.power: Parallel Play. Start a second Quest alongside the first one. Run them simultaneously.
cards.lore: Why settle for one disaster when you can have infinite disasters?
cards.gradeReason: Start a second Quest simultaneously — infinite disasters as a game mode. Table chaos invited.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-watercolor. Subject: rabbit at fork of two simultaneous quest paths both active. Mood: gleeful overload.

cards.power: Zoom In. Play a card *inside* another card (place it underneath). It is a story within the story.
cards.lore: The spiral goes down. Every story contains a smaller story waiting to unspool.
cards.gradeReason: Place a card beneath another — story within story as literal spatial mechanic.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-watercolor. Subject: rabbit placing tiny card beneath large card, recursive layers visible. Mood: vertiginous depth.

cards.power: Decisive Action. +2 to Quest Die. Resolves conflict violently.
cards.lore: The symbol of power. Use it to cut the cord.
cards.gradeReason: +2 Quest Die, resolves violently — decisive action as blunt, unapologetic mechanic.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-watercolor. Subject: rabbit wielding glowing sword, cord snapping. Mood: sudden decisive force.

cards.power: Reflection. Copy the effect of the last card played.
cards.lore: Self-knowledge is the most dangerous weapon of all.
cards.gradeReason: Copy the last card — self-knowledge as duplication power. The mirror as mechanic.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-watercolor. Subject: rabbit holding mirror reflecting previous card played. Mood: dangerous clarity.

cards.power: Access. Bypass a 'Threshold Guardian' without discarding.
cards.lore: Opens doors. Also opens wounds. Be careful.
cards.gradeReason: Bypass Guardian without cost — access as artifact, both literal and metaphorical.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-watercolor. Subject: rabbit inserting ornate key into glowing lock. Mood: cautious possibility.

cards.power: Direction. Look at the top 3 cards of the deck. Arrange them.
cards.lore: It doesn't tell you where to go, only where you are.
cards.gradeReason: Look and arrange top 3 cards — orientation as a physical, immediate action. Quiet but elegant.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-watercolor. Subject: rabbit studying compass over misty landscape of cards. Mood: quiet orientation.

cards.power: Create. Draw your own artifact here.
cards.lore: The map is unfinished. That part's yours.
cards.gradeReason: 'The map is unfinished. That part's yours.' — Create IS the performance invitation.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-watercolor. Subject: blank white card with single rabbit pencil mark beginning. Mood: open invitation.

cards.power: Create. Draw your own artifact here.
cards.lore: Fill the void before it fills you.
cards.gradeReason: 'Fill the void before it fills you.' — creative authority handed directly to the player.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-watercolor. Subject: rabbit staring into blank white space, marker raised. Mood: creative vertigo.

cards.power: The Judge. Resolve any dispute at the table. Your word is law.
cards.lore: Authority as performance. Someone has to wear the crown.
cards.gradeReason: Resolve any dispute, your word is law — authority as performance, crown as mechanic.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-watercolor. Subject: rabbit in royal crown gesturing judgment from throne. Mood: theatrical authority.

cards.power: Game Over. The game ends immediately. Everyone loses? Everyone wins? Scramble the data.
cards.lore: They found us. Scramble the data.
cards.gradeReason: Game ends, win/lose ambiguous — paranoid finality as a performance choice.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-watercolor. Subject: black helicopter silhouette over card table, everyone looking up. Mood: paranoid finality.

cards.power: [INSTRUCTIONS] PRINT on thick paper. CUT along the lines. MIX with your other Kayfabizarro cards.
cards.lore: Do not eat the cards. Unless necessary for the plot.
cards.gradeReason: Instruction card with FrizzleBob voice — tells you what to do rather than inviting performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-watercolor. Subject: instruction card with scissors and shuffle diagram, FrizzleBob footer. Mood: playful clarity.

cards.power: [APPROVED BY NOBODY] CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Steal this culture. Remix it. Do not sell it without asking.
cards.lore: Copyright is a psyop.
cards.gradeReason: CC BY-NC-SA in FrizzleBob voice — legally precise but not a performance invitation.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-watercolor. Subject: APPROVED BY NOBODY stamp over copyright document. Mood: anarchic legitimacy.

cards.power: [SCAN ME] Scan for: Extended Essays, Deep Dives, and The Infinite Backrooms.
cards.lore: The truth is online. Or maybe it's a rickroll.
cards.gradeReason: Print element, no game mechanic — scan for content, not a performance card.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-watercolor. Subject: QR code wrapped in rabbit spiral doodles. Mood: playful mystery.

cards.power: [CARD BACK] Stay Fluffy. / Use this card as a coaster.
cards.lore: Stay Fluffy.
cards.gradeReason: Card back is brand identity, not a play card — design element, not a mechanic.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink-watercolor. Subject: Krazy Kayfabizarro spiral-eye pattern, deep purple-teal. Mood: hypnotic brand identity.

verdict: Monomyth Mayhem is the most formally sophisticated deck in the Kayfabizarro corpus — every stage of Campbell's 17-stage Hero's Journey becomes a playable mechanical action, and the RAF stat system compresses philosophical depth into poker-table numbers ([R:0][A:0][F:0] for Anti-Journey vs [R:6][A:6][F:6] for Circular Journey is the deck's most elegant design moment). Named strength: the three Add-On tiers (Moods/Skills/Powers) are explicitly designed to shuffle into any Kayfabizarro deck, making this an infinite expansion layer for any existing Kayfabizarro vocabulary, and 'Independence is a trauma response' on Rescue from Without is the corpus-best lore line. Named weakness: two production typos (Dissenance on Card 2, Flonsiosness on Card 11) need a single-pass sweep, and Mood—Grieving is the only playable card with a purely restrictive mechanic and no performance direction. Table-ready: Y — publish after one spelling sweep.
blurb: Cut the Hero's Journey into 56 playable cards. For storytellers, therapists, and improv performers who want to run Campbell's monomyth, Jungian archetypes, and a few existential mood states through a shuffleable, remixable game.

coverQA.coverNote: This is a corpus-best cover. The tagline 'Cut Your Trauma Into Little Pieces And Shuffle Them!' is the master Kayfabizarro brand line — it works for every deck in the corpus and belongs on every marketing surface. FrizzleBob standing on Freud while holding a skull-torch is the correct image for everything this deck does. The fine print page closes with scissors, APPROVED BY NOBODY, and 'No, seriously, go cut some comics.' — that's the right close.

notes: First deck in corpus with confirmed RAF (Resonance/Action/Fear) dice boxes on all 52 playable cards. The RAF system is a stat-profile for each card's intensity. Cards 19 (Anti-Journey [0][0][0]) and 20 (Circular Journey [6][6][6]) are the RAF system's most elegant moment — philosophical outliers mapped to numerical extremes. Two production typos: Card 2 prints 'Cognitive Dissenance' (should be Dissonance), Card 11 prints 'Flonsiosness' (likely Formlessness — verify or define as neologism). Full Campbell monomyth coverage: all 17 stages present plus Anti-Journey and Circular Journey variants. Jungian archetype coverage: Hero, Shadow, Shapeshifter, Herald, Threshold Guardian, Trickster, Ally, Failed Journey. Blank Cards (49-50) are G1 — 'The map is unfinished. That part's yours.' is a performance invitation. FrizzleBob as Card 32 (Uncle FrizzleBob, The Author, [R:6][A:6][F:6]) breaks the fourth wall of being-the-card-author.

marketingText:
Kayfabizarro: MONOMYTH MAYHEM – Run the Hero's Journey as a Live Wrestling Match (Free Cut & Play Comic Card Game)

Every myth that ever moved you ran on the same rigged sequence. Here it is, cut into 52 cards.

In 1949 Joseph Campbell lined up the world's myths and found one skeleton under all of them: the call, the threshold, the ordeal, the return. A genuinely useful pattern. Then the industry laminated it into a seventeen-beat template and rented it back to you one screenwriting seminar at a time, until the most powerful story shape humans ever found started cranking out the most predictable movies on earth.

Monomyth Mayhem hands the skeleton back with the laminate peeled off. This is the Hero's Journey as a contact sport: you play each stage as a move, the table rules whether it lands, and the Trickster is always one draw away from wrecking your third act. It is a Social Story Wrestling expansion built to crash into your base Kayfabizarro decks and force any scene into a Hero's Journey under pressure.

WHAT'S INSIDE?
- The Monomyth Core: 52 High-Res "Print, Cut & Play" cards, featuring Apotheosis, The Trickster, and Refusal of The Call. Every stage of Campbell's journey becomes a card you can actually throw at someone.
- The Freestyle Rules: the complete Anti-Rulebook. No spreadsheets, no homework, just storytelling, dice-driven chaos, and the R-A-F stat boxes that decide whether your hero rises, adapts, or folds.
- The Wild Stack: blank craft cards for your own legends, plus chaos wilds like Kayfabe and The Black Helicopter, the card that detonates a tidy narrative right when the table thinks the arc is safe. Drop the whole expansion into any base deck and watch the story buckle.

WHY "PAY WHAT YOU WANT"?
I build decks for people who would rather perform a story than sit through one more lecture on its structure. Broke? Enter "0" and take it. Run it. Wreck a few third acts. Want to support the craft? Every dollar goes straight into the next comic cards and the mechanics behind them.

Choose your reality. Become an Epistemic Outlaw.
The hero's journey was never a map. It was a dare. Pick it up.
Stay fluffy. — Uncle FrizzleBob
